# sharepoint_theme_apply (Resource)

Applies a theme to a target site using the M365 CLI (m365 spo theme apply). This is a one-shot action, similar in spirit to null_resource with triggers: Terraform tracks whether apply has been run, not the resulting state of the target site. Deleting this resource only removes it from Terraform state — it does NOT revert the site to its previous theme. Changing theme_name or content_version re-runs apply.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Apply a custom theme; re-applied whenever the palette changes.
resource "sharepoint_theme_apply" "hr" {
  site_url        = "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/hr"
  theme_name      = sharepoint_theme.contoso_blue.name
  content_version = sharepoint_theme.contoso_blue.theme_hash
}

# Apply one of SharePoint's built-in themes.
resource "sharepoint_theme_apply" "projects" {
  site_url            = "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/projects"
  theme_name          = "Blue"
  is_sharepoint_theme = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `site_url` (String) Full URL of the target SharePoint site, e.g. https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/hr.
- `theme_name` (String) Name of the theme to apply: either a sharepoint_theme's name, or one of the standard SharePoint theme names (Blue, Orange, Red, Purple, Green, Gray, Dark Yellow, Dark Blue) when is_sharepoint_theme is true. Changing this re-runs apply with the new theme.

### Optional

- `content_version` (String) Opaque string used to detect when the applied theme's content has changed and should be re-applied. Typically set to a referenced sharepoint_theme's theme_hash. Changing this value re-applies the theme without replacing this resource.
- `is_sharepoint_theme` (Boolean) Set when theme_name refers to a standard SharePoint theme rather than a custom sharepoint_theme.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite resource ID: <site_url>|<theme_name>.
